fixed: THE GROUND STOPPED REPEATING, and it was two defects stacked. (1) The global-UV V step ran backwards on every global-mapped model in every pack, so every cell row was a half-texture tear; globalUvStep now measures the step off the model's own vertices, which also recovers two magnitudes the catalog has wrong (sea declares 0.5 and spans 0.25; lake_water_center declares 1 and spans 0.5). (2) Round 2's four-cell block phase traded the sheet's period for a GRID OF CUTS, and a grid of cuts is the rectangle four blind panels described. makeGroundScatterPatch moves the cut off the grid instead: the offset is chosen per region of a lattice rotated 31.7 degrees with a non-integer 2.9-cell period, and the lattice coordinate is jittered per texel so a region boundary is a ragged band rather than a line. One texture fetch, not three - the offset is applied to the coordinate, never blended between samples, because these sheets have twelve colours and a blend invents a thirteenth.

IT IS SAFE ONLY BECAUSE OF TWO FACTS THAT WERE CHECKED FIRST: the tile textures are NearestFilter on BOTH filters with generateMipmaps false, so a per-fragment UV discontinuity has no derivative to blow up and no mip level to jump; and RepeatWrapping is on, so any offset wraps. The offset is always whole texels, so the art never leaves the pixel grid.

varies() excluded `raised`, which classify.js sets from bounds.min[1] >= 0.5 - ELEVATION - when the silhouette test it wanted was `flat` (height < 0.02) and that clause was already on the line above. Measured with an A/B in the running page (sun.castShadow toggled off, same URL, tod 17.5, biome preset 'meadow'): sun-shadow transmission is 0.173 in encounter's showcase and 0.191 in simulation's - the two agree to 10%, so it is the rig and not the scene. The critic's 0.443 control was pokemon's painted contact-shadow decal (DECISIONS #18), which is a fixed-opacity quad and not a shadow-mapped shadow, so the two numbers were never comparable. Filing rather than working around: a scene cannot raise the fill without also raising the lit ground beside it. DECISIONS #39e.

coreRequests.want: tiles: a tall-grass model that tiles edge-to-edge, or a placement offset on Placement
coreRequests.why: `tall_grass` and `tall_grass_light` do not fill their cell, so a patch of them shows a grid of gaps whatever per-cell rotation and tint are applied - which is most of what makes a field read as a nursery at 2x. coreRequests.want: tools/assets: carry the V convention in the exporter — emit pack.bin UVs in the orientation three.js samples them, or write a `uvOrigin` field on the pack so the loader does not have to infer it per triangle
coreRequests.why: A .pdsts stores V measured down from the image top; three uploads with `flipY = true`. Nothing cancels, so every upright face in every generated pack has been sampling upside down since the first tileset loaded (DECISIONS #41a). `tiles` now corrects it at load with a per-triangle sign test gated to |ny| < 0.5, which is safe and measured — 608 of bw2-adastra's 2402 triangles, and the horizontal tiles diff byte-identical — but it cannot reach a face on a slope. The Pokemon Center sign is one: sign.png has the Poke Ball red-side-up and the building renders it white-side-up, at |ny| = 0.85. Widening the load-time gate to catch it would also flip 672 triangles of cliff bank and lake edge in AdAstra alone with no evidence they are wrong. In the exporter one rule covers every face at every angle and the loader pass can be deleted.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: set renderer.shadowMap.type explicitly to THREE.PCFShadowMap (or accept the substitution knowingly)
coreRequests.why: three r185 deprecates PCFSoftShadowMap and silently swaps in PCFShadowMap with a console warning. The substitution is not cosmetic: PCFShadowMap is the only branch of WebGLShadowMap that sets compareFunction on shadow.map.depthTexture, so the shadow map is a COMPARE_REF_TO_TEXTURE sampler and any module reading it must declare sampler2DShadow. Reading it as sampler2D drops the draw call silently - no console error, the draw still counted. environment lost most of a round to this. Naming the type in core makes the contract visible.
coreRequests.note: environment now does this at runtime in shadowFilter.js so the FIRST compiled program already carries SHADOWMAP_TYPE_PCF, but core/render.js:144 still asks for the deprecated constant and ARCHITECTURE §2.7 still documents it. Both should change.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: create the WebGLRenderer with stencil: true
coreRequests.why: Overlapping projected sprite shadows multiply (dst*shade twice) and the exact fix is one-fragment-per-pixel, which needs a stencil test. Without it the only idempotent option is depth-write from the shadow plane, and that occludes every transparent pass drawn after it (measured: it ate unrelated scene elements in a full-frame A/B). The compounding is small now that the shadows are the caster's own height, so this is a quality request, not a blocker. Cost is one stencil attachment on the main target.

coreRequests.want: the cave preset's ambient/exposure lifted so unlit rock is dark rather than (0,0,0), OR a way for a biome to register a wide, weak fill light that is not subject to environment/lamps.js's POOL_REACH 3.9 clamp
coreRequests.why: cave/pool is 12.43% and cave/close 16.23% of pixels at exactly (0,0,0), against docs/refs/02 at 0.00% and 04 at 0.06%. It is NOT shadows: --envNoShadow 1 on --showcase hunts --mode cave --preset close --tod 12 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the control, max channel delta 0 over 1,440,000 px (docs/progress/hunts/r4/ab/cave-close-12-noshadow.png vs -on.png), which also means round 3's open issue 'sun shadows are still cast inside the sealed cave' is wrong as written. And it is no longer albedo: hunts lifted the cold rock tint from 0x1f2740 to 0x6c7691 this round and the pool frame only came from 27.29% to 12.43%, because instanceColor multiplies and a near-black bw2-cave set3 texel stays near black however white the tint. hunts owns lamp placement and has eleven bulbs down there, but lamps.js clamps every PointLight's reach to POOL_REACH 3.9 world units whatever radius is asked for, so a biome physically cannot fill a 56x54 room with placed light. This is the last thing between the cave and ref02's 0.194 mean saturation / 254 p99.  Related and NOT a re-file: coreRequests #27 and #35 already ask for a less saturated, less warm cave preset (the fog is 0x4a2f18 at density 0.040 with `saturation: 1.30`), and this round moved mean saturation on the default framing from a round-2 control's 0.588 to 0.516 without touching any of that — so #35 still stands and is still the larger term. This request is only about the *black*: 12-16% of the frame at exactly (0,0,0) against references at 0.00% and 0.06%.

coreRequests.want: A shadow that fades with distance from its caster, in core/render.js - either a second depth channel carrying the caster distance, or a cheap approximation such as attenuating the shadow term by the receiver depth minus the shadow-map depth.
coreRequests.why: The oldest open visual defect in the project (four rounds) is caster-less slabs at low sun. Round 6 isolated it: they are real, correctly alpha-tested tree shadows from casters standing outside the frame, raked 6.6x by an 8.64-degree shown sun at tod 17.5 and 16.6x at 18:00 (?envCasterOff=tree,pine removes 100% of them). Every fix available to a module was built and measured and costs more than the defect - capping the shadow run by raising the key elevation floor costs forest-17.5 mean 38.8->64.8, and shallowing the shadow costs it 41->60, because a wood at dusk IS its long shadows. Fading a shadow with distance from its caster keeps the short contact shadow that reads and drops the 25-unit ribbon that does not, and it is the one lever a preset cannot reach.  [WITHDRAWN BY environment ROUND 8, DECISIONS #54(a). No core change is needed. A comparison sampler will not RETURN a blocker depth, but it will answer "is the blocker nearer to the light than this?" as often as you like, so the distance is probed with a ladder of references: a tap lit at z-t means t >= d, and the lit-count over K rungs is K - d/dt. Two accumulators over an 8-tap search disk give the average blocker distance with no depth value ever leaving the sampler, and no second depth channel. Shipped in src/environment/shadowFilter.js at 8x(5+1)+24 = 72 fetches per pixel, measured at 0.1 ms of p95 at 1080p.]

coreRequests.want: Either document that colour-valued grade uniforms (lift/gain) are converted sRGB->linear by THREE.Color, or add a display-space colour helper to core/config.js.
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #50(a): presets.js authors lift as a display-space hex because that is what a post-tonemap offset is, but new THREE.Color(hex) with ColorManagement on delivers it in linear - 0x191c28 arrives as (2.5,3.0,5.4)/255, not (25,28,40). Two rounds raised the night lift against contrast's crush point using the hex bytes and moved nothing, and the frames measured 4.6-8.4% of pixels at exactly rgb(0,0,0). This is a trap any module writing a colour uniform can fall into.

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: take over the soft-shadow filter. environment currently replaces THREE.ShaderChunk.shadowmap_pars_fragment at init (src/environment/shadowFilter.js) with a 24-tap Vogel PCF plus a receiver-plane depth bias, because three's shipped 5 taps dither the whole lawn at any radius wide enough to matter. §2.7 says the look lives in core; this is a runtime tune in a module folder and it should move, together with `renderer.shadowMap.type = PCFShadowMap` and a documented default for `light.shadow.radius`.
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #52(a-c). Measured: the 90->10% shadow transition goes 3 px -> 26 px, gate 6 improved / 0 regressed, 60 fps and identical draw calls on all twelve frames.  [UPDATED BY environment ROUND 8: the chunk is no longer a 24-tap Vogel PCF at one radius per frame. It is PCSS - an 8-tap x 5-rung ladder probe of the comparison sampler estimates the blocker distance per pixel and sets the kernel from it, with light.shadow.radius re-read as the WIDEST penumbra this hour. It also needs the sun shadow camera's far-near at install time, which is why environment.init calls three.sun.update({x:0,y:0,z:0}) first: at init the camera is still three's default 0.5..500 and baking that against the real 167.5 makes every blocker distance three times short. If this moves into core it should take that calibration with it. DECISIONS #54(a).]

coreRequests.want: core/render.js: give `contrast` a soft toe instead of a hard clamp. It is `(x - 0.5) * c + 0.5`, so it has a crush point at `0.5 - 0.5/c` and everything under it becomes exactly 0 — 0.1173 at the golden hour's c = 1.307. A smoothstep toe over the bottom of the range would cost the black point almost nothing and would stop a warm frame's blue channel being clamped away.
coreRequests.why: 48.5% of hunts/forest/17.5 has blue at exactly 0, against 1.17% in docs/refs/04 at the same mean blue (30.2). Proven NOT to be the shadow: inside the shadow mask it is 50.5% against 48.5% frame-wide, and in city/high-street/17.5 the shadow is less zero-blue than the frame (10.5% vs 20.0%). Every preset-side fix was shot and priced in DECISIONS #52(f) and all of them cost more than the defect. This is #50(a)'s crush point, one layer deeper.

coreRequests.want: hunts: the cave floor lays two sheets that are 2x apart in mean luminance in the same field

Laid in one field those two read as a hard two-level checkerboard whatever tiles does to either of them: a per-cell tone jitter is a few percent and this is a factor of two. Note also that src/hunts/biomes/cave.js:97 computes `floorModels` and never uses it. tiles can extend varies() to category 'cave' so the cave floor gets tone and phase like every other floor - say the word and it is two characters - but that cannot close a 2x sheet difference, so the palette choice has to move first.

coreRequests.want: nothing — recorded so it is not re-filed
coreRequests.why: DECISIONS #18 filed `config.cameraDistance: 30` as a coreRequest because a sprite texel lands on 1.62 internal pixels there, and 24.365 is where it lands on exactly two. That request is CLOSED WITHOUT THE CHANGE: DECISIONS #58 makes the magnification a whole number at whatever distance the camera is at, per sprite per frame, which is what was actually asked for and does not pin the framing. 24.365 remains the distance where the new snap is a no-op, and the showcases still use it.

coreRequests.want: DONE — pixelsPerUnit is the primitive, and the camera is orthographic (DECISIONS #60)
coreRequests.why: User report: "Some screens have the trainer, pokemons and npcs assets bigger... perfect pixel that dont change when im walking neither on trainers, structures or props. All pixelart environments sometimes create additional borders or lose the core definition." unitsPerPixel was an OUTPUT of the window size (2*D*tan(fov/2)/internalHeight), so it was 26.0 px/unit at 1080p, 23.7 on a 1512-wide laptop and 17.4 at 1280x720. field.js rounds that to a whole magnification, so the cast was drawn at k=0.68 on a laptop and k=1.23 on a monitor - an 82% spread, discontinuous. 32-texel tile art was minified by a different fraction on every screen, and which texel rows NEAREST dropped changed as the camera moved. Locking the density is necessary and not sufficient: under perspective at pitch 45 / fov 26 the ground runs 0.75x at the top of the frame to 1.20x at the bottom, so only one horizontal row could ever be pixel-exact. Orthographic makes unitsPerPixel depth-independent, so the one camera snap grids the entire frame and a walk is a whole-pixel translation. Also fixed: lookAt aimed at 42.77 degrees, not cameraPitch 45, and sprites.js cancels the foreshortening with 1/cos(45) - every sprite was 3.9% too tall with non-square texels. And resize() produced odd buffers, where the world snapped to pixel centres and the sprites to edges; both dimensions are even now and the phaseX/phaseY workaround is gone. Cost: zoom is a three-rung ladder (16/32/64 - the only densities where 16-texel sprites and 32-texel tiles are both whole), so ~40 biome framings that differed by a few tiles of camera distance now differ only by their marker. Both pixelExactDistance() copies deleted. 1080p frames 20 tiles across, not 24; targetInternalWidth is the knob.

integratorFindings.topic: coast: the shoreline staircase with no surf (hunts' open issue #8)
integratorFindings.verdict: CONFIRMED, still present after the round-2 fix, and the cause is now pinned. Cropped the deep/shallow boundary at 2x: long axis-aligned runs meeting at right angles with no transition tile of any kind, while the sand/grass boundary one band below it scallops correctly because it is autotiled.
integratorFindings.cause: `deep = water.clone().shrink(3)` is an erosion, and eroding by 3 removes every one-cell feature, so the deep-water region is a SMOOTHED copy of the coastline — which quantised onto the grid is a clean staircase. The deep region is then laid as flat cells with no border family, so its edge is blocky whatever shape it has.
integratorFindings.triedAndReverted: fraying the deep edge after the erosion (ragged 0.5 / period 3, despeckle 4). It makes it worse: without border tiles, every frayed cell is another hard rectangle, so the edge goes from a straight staircase to floating dark-blue blocks. Looked at it, reverted it.
integratorFindings.theActualFix: bw2-adastra ships a complete 13-slot `walk_edge` family — corners, edges and inner corners — tagged `foam` and `surf`, and it is not being used on this boundary at all. The model named `sea` has no border family, so the deep water can only ever be blocky on its own; the foam belongs to the shallows and should ring the wadeable region on BOTH its edges, against the land and against the deep. That is hunts/biomes/coast.js's to make.

integratorFindings.topic: the mirrored set0 transition slots (hunts' coreRequest: 'the V-convention belongs in the exporter')
integratorFindings.verdict: THE MIRROR IS REAL and I confirmed it independently of hunts: for grass_path_side_edge_w the vertex at world (0,0) — the WEST corner — carries u=0.0 and the east corner u=1.0, so U runs backwards against world X. The cause is the same one DECISIONS #5 records for winding: converting PDSMS's Z-up/Y-south space swaps two axes, which is a mirror, and the winding was realigned for it while the texture coordinates were not. Almost nothing shows it because ground, cliff and water art is tiling or near-symmetric; the transition slots are neither.
integratorFindings.triedAndReverted: flipping U in tools/assets/pdsts.js and rebuilding all 13 packs. The regression gate came back 1 improved / 0 regressed — but the gate measures histograms, not layout, so I scanned the road directly. The green ribbon splitting the path went from 6px to 16px: WORSE. hunts already ships a compensating 180-degree rotation on those two slots (SET0_OUTWARD in src/hunts/palette.js), so fixing the exporter double-corrects them.
integratorFindings.theActualFix: exporter and workaround must move together, in one change: flip U in pdsts.js, rebuild every pack, and delete SET0_OUTWARD in the same commit. Worth doing because the workaround cannot reach the four outer and four inner corner slots — their art is diagonal, and a quarter turn moves it to the wrong diagonal — which is why the road still breaks at every meander step. That is a coordinated tools+hunts change and belongs in one commissioned round, not in an integrator patch to one half of it.
integratorFindings.alsoLearned: the gate has a blind spot worth naming: it reduces frames to luminance and saturation histograms, so it catches brightness, crush and performance regressions and is silent on composition. A layout defect still needs a scanline or an eye.
integratorFindings.secondAttempt: Tried the coordinated version too — flip U in the exporter AND delete SET0_OUTWARD in the same change, which was my own prescription. Road scanline at y=700, interior green gaps: workaround only [6px], exporter only [16px], BOTH [16px, 15px]. The coordinated fix is the worst of the three. So the U mirror is real but it is NOT what causes the ribbons, and my prescription was wrong. Both halves reverted; the shipped state (workaround only, 6px) is the best of the three.
integratorFindings.whatIsActuallyLeft: hunts' own critic already had this right and I should have believed it: 'SET0_OUTWARD turns edge_w/edge_e only; the corner cases are deliberately left mirrored, so each step stamps a green grass comma INSIDE the tan.' The residual gaps are at MEANDER STEPS — the eight corner slots — whose art is diagonal, so neither a 180-degree turn nor a U flip can place it correctly. That needs per-slot handling, not a global convention change.
